A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PRISM study. Their text, equations, four tables, five figures, and Appendices A–H are readable and matchable; the shorter v2 reflects reflow rather than missing material.

before.justification: v1 reports original WebShop and ALFWorld experiments, routing ablations, computational measurements, and appendix robustness analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Tables 1–4, Figures 3–5, and Appendices B, D, and G.

M1.justification: Sections 2.2–2.4 retain frozen-model gradient probing, matrix-wise Frobenius norms, Gini/kurtosis/CV concentration measures, and median-based routing to SFT or RL. No algorithmic component or training objective changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use WebShop and ALFWorld, including the same ALFWorld Seen/Unseen evaluations and six household task categories. Section 3.1 and Appendix E introduce no additional domains or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain the same base-model, SFT, GRPO, GiGPO, Random, HPT, and SFT-then-RL comparisons. Figure 3 retains inverse allocation, and Table 4 retains gradient-magnitude routing.

E3.justification: The backbones, allocation ratios, evaluation metrics, and training procedures remain unchanged. Appendix C retains the same context lengths, optimization settings, rollout size, rewards, and episode-step limits.

E4.justification: Both versions retain routing reversal, magnitude-versus-concentration comparisons, allocation-ratio sensitivity, qualitative trajectory inspection, metric-consensus analysis, and parameter-count normalization robustness checks (Section 4; Appendices B, D, G).

E5.justification: Section 3.1 reports means across three random seeds in both versions. Figure 4 retains identical 90% confidence-interval bands; no additional uncertainty reporting or statistical procedure appears.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and Figures 3–5 retain their values and findings. PRISM (Gini) still reports 95.31%/79.69% ALFWorld Seen/Unseen success and a maximum 3.22× speedup; Appendix G still reports Spearman’s rho above 0.99.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and the concentration definitions in Appendix A are unchanged. Appendix F’s mechanistic argument and Appendix G’s invariance reasoning are also retained without new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about gradient concentration diagnosing conflict, allocating consolidation to SFT and adaptation to RL, and achieving superior performance with up to 3.22× speedup.

C2.justification: The mechanism interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged. Section 7 retains limitations concerning model scale, static routing, and generalization beyond agentic benchmarks; the appendix explanations are preserved.

D1.justification: v2 adds a public-source-code statement and PRISM repository address to the abstract, absent from v1. Existing implementation settings, hardware disclosures, and training-time information are unchanged; repository contents are not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: The Llama backbone citation changes from AI@Meta’s Llama 3 model card to Grattafiori et al.’s The Llama 3 Herd of Models. This is a limited source replacement; Section 5’s research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 8, Acknowledgements, and the abstract’s code-access sentence, corrects author-list punctuation, reduces listed contact addresses, and updates bibliographic details. The scientific narrative and appendix prose are otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Spacing and page flow change: Limitations starts on page 8 instead of page 9, and the final appendix material fits on page 13. Figures and tables retain their designs, labels, captions, and content.

improvement.justification: The new source-code address fills a useful access-information gap in v1, modestly improving reproducibility documentation. Author/reference corrections and reduced blank space provide small presentation benefits. The scientific methods, evidence, and limitations remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
